title: Write unit tests for RemoteManager staging methods
description:
## Overview

Write unit tests for the new RemoteManager staging and committing methods in `tests/test_remote.py`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Test `stage_all()` stages all files
- [ ] Test `commit()` creates a commit with the provided message
- [ ] Test `has_staged_changes()` returns True when changes are staged
- [ ] Test `has_staged_changes()` returns False when no changes are staged
- [ ] Test `has_unstaged_changes()` returns True when untracked/modified files exist
- [ ] Test `has_unstaged_changes()` returns False when no untracked/modified files exist
- [ ] Test git command failures raise appropriate exceptions
- [ ] All tests use mocking to avoid actual git operations

## Files to Create/Modify

- `tests/test_remote.py` - Add tests for new RemoteManager methods
- Use `unittest.mock.patch` or `pytest-mock` to mock subprocess calls

## Test Pattern Example

```python
def test_stage_all(self, mock_run_git):
    manager = RemoteManager(Path("/tmp/repo"))
    manager.stage_all()
    mock_run_git.assert_called_once_with(["add", "-A"], cwd=Path("/tmp/repo"))
```

title: Add staging and committing methods to RemoteManager
description:
## Overview

Add staging and committing methods to RemoteManager class in `src/dotman/remote.py`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Add `stage_all()` method that runs `git add -A` (respects .gitignore)
- [ ] Add `commit(message: str)` method that runs `git commit -m <message>`
- [ ] Add `has_staged_changes()` method that checks for staged changes
- [ ] Add `has_unstaged_changes()` method that checks for unstaged changes
- [ ] All methods use the existing `_run_git_command()` infrastructure
- [ ] Methods raise appropriate exceptions on git command failures

## Files to Modify

- `src/dotman/remote.py` - Add new methods to RemoteManager class

## Technical Notes

- `git add -A` stages all new, modified, and deleted files (respects .gitignore)
- Use `git diff --cached --quiet` to check for staged changes (returncode 0 = no changes)
- Use `git diff --quiet` to check for unstaged changes
- Handle subprocess errors appropriately

title: Update CLI push command with auto-stage and stage-only flag
description:
## Overview

Update the CLI push command in `src/dotman/cli.py` to automatically stage all changes, commit with auto-generated timestamped message, and push by default. Add `--stage-only` flag for staging without pushing.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Add `--stage-only` / `-s` flag to the push command
- [ ] Default behavior (no flags): Stage all → Commit with auto-generated message → Push
- [ ] With `--stage-only`: Stage all → Commit with auto-generated message → Stop (don't push)
- [ ] Auto-generated commit message format: `dotman update: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS ZZZZ`
- [ ] Timezone info uses standard format (e.g., `+0530` for IST, `-0800` for PST)
- [ ] When no changes exist: Print "[yellow]No changes to commit.[/yellow]" and exit 0
- [ ] When staging succeeds but commit fails: Show error and exit with code 1
- [ ] When commit succeeds but push fails: Show "Changes staged and committed but push failed" error
- [ ] When push succeeds after staging/committing: Print "[green]Successfully pushed to remote![/green]"
- [ ] When `--stage-only` completes: Print "[green]Changes staged and committed![/green]"
- [ ] All existing push command options (remote, branch, set-upstream) must continue to work

## Files to Modify

- `src/dotman/cli.py` - Update push() function with new options and logic
- `src/dotman/remote.py` - Ensure new methods are available

## Commit Message Format

```python
from datetime import datetime
message = f"dotman update: {datetime.now().astimezone().strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S %z')}"
# Example output: "dotman update: 2026-01-19 14:30:45 +0530"
```

title: Write integration tests for push command
description:

- [ ] Test default push behavior: stages, commits, and pushes changes

## Files to Create

- `tests/test_cli_push.py` - Integration tests for push command

## Test Approach

- Use temporary git repositories (tmpdir) for testing
- Use `subprocess` to run actual git commands in test repos
- Test the full CLI command flow using `typer.testing.CliRunner`

## Example Test Structure

```python
from typer.testing import CliRunner
from dotman.cli import app

def test_push_with_staging_and_commit(tmp_path):
    # Setup: create temp git repo with changes
    # Run: dotman push
    # Assert: changes are staged, committed, and pushed
```

Note: This test file is new and should follow the project's testing patterns from `tests/conftest.py`.

title: Auto-stage and commit for dotman push
description:
## Overview

Modify the `dotman push` command to automatically stage all changes (respecting `.gitignore`), generate a timestamped commit message, and push to the remote. This makes the push workflow more automatic and user-friendly by eliminating the need for manual `git add` commands.

## Goals

- Eliminate the need for users to manually run `git add` before `dotman push`
- Automatically generate meaningful commit messages with timestamps and timezone
- Provide a `--stage-only` flag for users who want to stage and commit without pushing
- Ensure all changes are properly committed before pushing to avoid partial updates

## Quality Gates

These commands must pass for every user story:
1. `ruff check .` - Linting (fix auto-fixable issues first, then verify)
2. `ruff format .` - Code formatting
3. `mypy .` - Type checking
4. `pytest -v` - All tests must pass (unit + integration)
5. `coverage report --fail-under=80` - Coverage threshold check

## Tasks in this Epic

1. dotman-5o0: Add staging and committing methods to RemoteManager
2. dotman-auw: Add NothingToCommitError exception
3. dotman-81g: Update CLI push command with auto-stage and stage-only flag
4. dotman-0k8: Write unit tests for RemoteManager staging methods
5. dotman-a2o: Write integration tests for push command

## Dependency Graph

```
dotman-5o0 (RemoteManager methods)
    │
    ├──► dotman-auw (NothingToCommitError)
    │         │
    │         ▼
    ├──► dotman-81g (CLI push command) ◄─── depends on both above
    │         │
    │         ▼
    ├──► dotman-0k8 (Unit tests) ◄───────── depends on dotman-5o0
    │
    ▼
dotman-a2o (Integration tests) ◄───────── depends on dotman-81g
```
